newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes values off, eyes on India, Bangchak.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes values off, eyes on India, Bangchak.

text.p: Asian crude prices edged lower in a quiet market on Thursday but could be supported on Friday by firming Brent futures prices.
Traders said three more Oman deals emerged with trades in a range of MPM +13 cents to plus 13.5 cents, slightly lower than the previous high of plus 15 cents seen on Wednesday.
Traders said they heard one million barrels of January Masila traded between majors at dated Brent less 98 cents.
Some traders wondered if the Masila had December dates as term prices for the first quarter were still under consideration.
Elsewhere, paper levels were mostly steady taking their cue from the latest overnight numbers out of the U.S. market.
January Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.75/$1.80 per barrel, under pressure from the strength of the Dubai market.
The January/February Dubai spread was assessed at a steady 55/60 cents and February/March at 52/56.
Further Dubai indications came in the offers into the India tender to buy January crude.
A major offered a Dubai cargo at half month quotes plus 65 cents, and a trader offered a cargo at half month quotes plus 68 cents.
Traders said the offers indicated a value on the basis of full month quotes above 80 cents. The last wet cargo traded for January was at full-month quotes plus 80 cents.
The India tender is expected to be awarded later on Thursday.
Traders were also watching the Bangchak refinery crude tender, which is also due to be awarded later on Thursday.
